Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: RequestErrorRate on frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom of a broken cart-to-Redis path, not a frontend-proxy fault. frontend-proxy's error spans are all on its 'ingress' operation and are HTTP 504s at ~15 s; the sampled traces show the 15 s proxy deadline expiring while the frontend's /api/cart API route runs ~490-500 s and returns HTTP 500, and while cart's gRPC spans fail with gRPC status 9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis" at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(). cart's own pod logs repeat "Wasn't able to connect to redis" from 09:06:15 onward, and cart's Redis command spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE, ~620-1370 per 5m before) fall to zero while cart error spans appear; frontend and checkout carry their own cart-call error spans. The error onset is between 09:05 and 09:06 (proxy ingress 5m error increase 0 at 09:05, 53.3 at 09:06, 421.4 at 09:10), matching the alert start 09:05:56. cart and valkey-cart pods are both Running, Ready and never restarted, valkey's container stayed far below its 10Mi limit, valkey-cart's Service/endpoints resolve to its pod IP, and the collector's redis receiver keeps receiving INFO data from valkey after 09:06 (memory used flat at 1,710,360 bytes, cpu time flat at 2.6249 s) - so "valkey crashed or was OOM-killed" is not supported. The deepest point the evidence reaches is a loss of connectivity between the cart pod and valkey-cart:6379 at ~09:05, which is reported as a hypothesis because the network-policy/datapath objects that could explain it are not readable here, so no single Kubernetes object can be named as the origin of the fault.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress error spans were at background level (~1-3 per 5m) through 09:05, then jumped to 53.3 (09:06), 170 (09:07), 284.4 (09:08), 393.3 (09:09) and 421.4 (09:10) per 5m, while ingress non-error (UNSET) spans fell from ~3023 per 5m at 09:05 to ~1025 at 09:10.

Wasn't able to connect to redis" - so frontend's failures are its cart calls.

Per-service 15m error-span increases at 09:20 include cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 45.23 and GetCart 38.77, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 46.31 and GetCart 31.93, frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 80.35, checkout oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 6.75 and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 6.75, and frontend-proxy ingress 916.80; checkout's only error spans are on its cart calls and PlaceOrder.

The cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logs "Wasn't able to connect to redis" repeatedly from 2026-11-17T09:06:15.139444Z (the first match in the 08:50-09:06:30 window) through 09:12:32, each followed by "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.".

cart's log shows normal per-second AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync lines until 09:04:41.5429411Z, then no cart log line at all for ~56 s, with logging resuming at 09:05:37.5682448Z and the first Redis connection failure at 09:06:15.139444Z.

cart's Redis command spans stop: HGET went from 1311-1372 per 5m (09:00-09:05), HMSET and EXPIRE from ~581-649 per 5m, and its server spans (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart ~870-884, AddItem ~442-483) to 0 in the 09:10 and 09:15 buckets, while STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for AddItem (12.5 then 31.1) and GetCart (10 then 26.7) appeared in those same buckets.

The cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 (owned by ReplicaSet cart-755465879b, Deployment cart) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 08:32:55, and has no previous terminated container; the valkey-cart pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is likewise Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 08:32:53.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo has every fault-injection flag at defaultVariant "off", including cartFailure ("Fail cart service"), so the cart failure is not being injected through the cartFailure flagd flag.

valkey-cart answering the collector's Redis INFO scrapes (memory and cpu time reported, cpu time flat at 2.6249 s, memory used flat at 1,710,360 bytes) after 09:06 contradicts the hypothesis that the valkey-cart process crashed, stopped listening or was OOM-killed during this incident; its container also shows no restart.

Resource exhaustion on the valkey-cart side is not supported as the cause: its peak cgroup usage was 5.95 MB of a 10Mi limit, its working set stayed 3.5-3.9 MB, its CPU usage was only 0.0023-0.0030 cores and its CFS throttle ratio 0.016-0.061 across the window.

Second candidate: cart-side saturation contributes to the connection failures - cart's CFS throttle ratio rose from 0.17-0.24 to 0.76 (09:10) and 0.89 (09:15) and its working set from ~57 MB to ~95 MB right at onset; this is not established as causal because its CPU usage (~0.022 cores) stayed well below its 45m limit and the throttle increase accompanies the error/retry burst.

Inspect Cilium state and flows for the cart pod (100.96.2.233) and valkey-cart pod (100.96.2.228:6379) - CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumEndpoint objects and hubble flows for drops on port 6379 - and test DNS resolution plus a TCP connect to valkey-cart:6379 from the cart pod; those are the checks that can confirm or refute the leading connectivity hypothesis.

Add a readiness/liveness probe to the valkey-cart container and raise or remove its 10m CPU / 10Mi memory limits, since the Deployment currently has no probe at all and Ready therefore says nothing about Redis being able to serve cart.

gaps: CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumEndpoint objects and hubble flow data are not readable with the available resource kinds, so whether a network policy or datapath fault dropped cart->valkey-cart packets cannot be determined, and no object can be named as the origin of that fault.

The collector's redisreceiver exposes only cpu/memory metrics, not connected_clients or keyspace statistics, so whether valkey rejected cart's new connections cannot be verified.
The NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota queries returned no objects, and those views are not citable as fact, so the absence of policy/quota objects in otel-demo is unconfirmed.
Prometheus data available to these queries ends around 09:12-09:16 (data_as_of), so the state after that and the recovery point are unknown.

The change-history integration is not integrated, so it is unknown why the whole otel-demo namespace was rolled out at 08:32:44-08:34:30, ~33 minutes before onset, and whether any object (deployment, policy, service) was changed at ~09:05.
